title: Milky Way over Paranal
caption: The Milky Way over the Very Large Telescope, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: A trail of lights leads toward Cerro Paranal, where ESO's Very Large Telescope sits on the summit. Above the observatory, the familiar glow of the Milky Way, marked by dark lanes of dust, seems to reach down and touch the telescopes. In the lower left of the image are the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds.

The VLT is ESO's flagship observatory, and this view places it beneath the galaxy it studies. The dark lanes in the Milky Way are clouds of dust that block the light of the stars behind them, cutting the bright band into patches.

The Magellanic Clouds are small companion galaxies of the Milky Way, visible only from the southern half of the world. They are separate systems, each full of stars of its own, lying outside our galaxy.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera at Paranal. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long exposure gathers far more light than the eye, so the Milky Way and the Magellanic Clouds appear brighter here than they would in person.

explore: The trail of lights on the approach to the summit gives a sense of scale: the telescopes are tiny beside the sweep of the sky above them. The Magellanic Clouds appear at lower left.
alt: A line of lights leading up to telescopes on a mountaintop, with the Milky Way above and two faint cloud-like galaxies at lower left.
